READING

**The problem in numbers**

Fennerbrake packs 18 pallets a day and collects every four days, so the standing stock at peak is up to 72 pallet spaces. The current 25 % entitlement at Wildern Cross gives 52 spaces — 20 short. The July 2026 shortfall cost £45,136 (18,200 kg × £2.48 loss per kg between retail and processor price), and there is no reason to expect a different result in July 2027 under the status quo.

Both courses fix the physical capacity problem: HAVERSHOLT gives 104 spaces (32 of surplus), TREGOWAN gives 52 on-site plus 30 off-site (10 of surplus, but split across two sites). The question is which is better over time, and whether HAVERSHOLT's risk profile is tolerable.

---

**TREGOWAN: annual cost and a commercial threat**

The direct annual charge is £24,000 rent plus £7,200 haulage = £31,200 every season, recurring indefinitely. Against the £45,136 baseline loss, that yields a net annual benefit of only £13,936, and every year the charges are paid again from scratch.

More seriously, the buyer has already queried the extra handling. Fourteen miles of refrigerated haulage introduces extra touch-points, food miles, and slight temperature variation. If the buyer responds by reducing the accepted price — even a few pence per kilogram across a season's tonnage — the entire net benefit disappears, and the downside could exceed the baseline loss. The problem states Fennerbrake's price is £3.10/kg; a 5 p reduction on the full pack (say 300 tonnes in a season) would cost £15,000 alone. TREGOWAN does nothing about the contention at Wildern Cross, and at 25 % Fennerbrake is outvoted on everything including the timing and specification of the compressor replacement.

---

**HAVERSHOLT: economics**

Purchase cost: £96,000. Capital remaining: £44,000.

Compressor: the £260,000 bill falls pro-rata within three years. At 25 % that is £65,000; at 50 % it is £130,000 — an additional £65,000. Total additional capital commitment versus staying at 25 %: £96,000 + £65,000 = £161,000.

Against that, HAVERSHOLT saves £31,200 a year compared with TREGOWAN (no rent, no haulage). Breakeven on £161,000 at £31,200 a year is just over five years. After year five every season TREGOWAN charges £31,200 and HAVERSHOLT charges nothing. The comparison improves further if the buyer's quality concern under TREGOWAN ever bites into the £3.10 price.

The compressor timing creates cash pressure: £44,000 on hand after purchase, then up to £130,000 needed within three years. But the annual processor-loss saving (roughly £45,000) feeds back into the business from July 2027 onwards. Over three seasons that is around £135,000, which more than closes the gap, albeit without certainty. It is tight, not fatal. Fennerbrake also now holds 50 % of the votes on when and how the compressor is replaced — which matters if there is room to phase expenditure or choose a lower-cost specification.

---

**HAVERSHOLT: pre-emption risk**

Ardwick has 30 days to match. The important question is whether they would want to.

Ardwick currently holds 50 % = 104 spaces and pays 50 % of any capex. If they pre-empt:

- They pay £96,000 for Wraysholme's 25 %.
- Their compressor share rises from 50 % (£130,000) to 75 % (£195,000).
- Total incremental outlay: £96,000 + £65,000 = £161,000 for a store in which they already have comfortable headroom and a majority.

There is no obvious operational gain for Ardwick. Their peak runs concurrently with Fennerbrake's, so they cannot use Fennerbrake's theoretical spare spaces. The extra stake buys them voting dominance they nearly already have (outvoting a 25 % partner at 50 % is already straightforward on most ordinary resolutions). For £161,000 of cash and compressor exposure, the benefit to Ardwick is thin. The risk of pre-emption is real — Ardwick are not obliged to be rational — but the financial incentive to exercise it is weak.

Critically, even if Ardwick does pre-empt, the TREGOWAN fallback remains available: Ilsington Chilled must be booked by 2027-03-31, and Ardwick's 30-day window (triggered on or before 2026-11-30) resolves by late December 2026 at the latest, leaving three months to secure the Ilsington booking. Attempting HAVERSHOLT does not foreclose TREGOWAN.

---

**HAVERSHOLT: strategic value**

At 50 %, Fennerbrake holds half the votes on the store's future: compressor timing, any future capital works, future share sales. At 25 %, Ardwick (50 %) can carry any resolution alone. Governance is not a luxury on a facility where a £260,000 bill is already visible and the compressors are seventeen years old.

---

**Summary judgment**

TREGOWAN is a safe short-term fix but not a safe long-term position: it costs £31,200 a year forever, it brings buyer quality risk that could erode the core selling price, it leaves Fennerbrake outvoted at the store, and it never builds any asset. HAVERSHOLT is capital-intensive and has a pre-emption risk, but the financial incentive for Ardwick to pre-empt is poor, the cumulative economics overtake TREGOWAN before year six, the buyer concern is eliminated, and a 50 % stake gives equal votes on a facility whose next large cost event is already known.

---

READING
  The shortfall is 20 pallet spaces (72 required, 52 entitled). July 2026 cost: £45,136 (18,200 kg × £2.48). Both courses fix capacity; the choice turns on long-run cost, risk, and commercial exposure.

  TREGOWAN costs £31,200 a year indefinitely. Against the £45,136 baseline saving, that is only £13,936 net benefit annually — and it is at risk because the buyer has already flagged concern about extra handling at fourteen miles. Any price concession on the core £3.10/kg rate erodes or reverses that net benefit, with no exit except abandoning the rental.

  HAVERSHOLT's total extra capital commitment (£96,000 purchase + £65,000 extra compressor share) is £161,000. At £31,200 saved per year versus TREGOWAN, the breakeven is just over five years, after which every season favours HAVERSHOLT. The compressor gap (£130,000 due within three years, only £44,000 available after purchase) is tight but serviceable: the annual process-loss saving of ~£45,000 runs from July 2027 and covers the shortfall within three seasons, and the 50 % vote gives Fennerbrake equal say over compressor timing.

  Pre-emption by Ardwick: exercising the right would cost Ardwick £96,000 plus an extra £65,000 on the compressor (from £130,000 to £195,000) for governance control they near-enough already hold at 50 %. The financial deterrent is substantial. Even if they do pre-empt, Ilsington Chilled's March 2027 booking deadline is well clear of Ardwick's late-December resolution window, so the TREGOWAN fallback remains open.

  At 50 %, Fennerbrake holds half the votes on future capex and policy at a store where a large and imminent bill is already identified. At 25 %, Ardwick can outvote Fennerbrake unilaterally.

CALL
  HAVERSHOLT

GROUNDS
  Ardwick's pre-emption would add £65,000 to their own compressor liability on top of £96,000 for a stake that gives them little they do not already hold, making pre-emption financially unattractive, while TREGOWAN's £31,200 annual charge compounds indefinitely, its extra handling has drawn direct buyer concern, and HAVERSHOLT's cumulative cost advantage becomes decisive before year six.
